data.title: Compensation Double Bind
data.content:
# Compensation Double Bind

The candidate has to name a compensation expectation first: a high number ends the process, and a low one lowers the level the candidate is assessed at.

### Trigger Rule
The candidate is asked for a compensation number before the band for the role is stated, and the band is not stated in return.

### What this Establishes
- An information asymmetry works as an uncalibrated filter before technical merit is assessed.

### What this Does NOT Establish
- Does not establish that the employer has an unlimited budget, or that any of this is malicious.

specimens.label: The asymmetry, in four messages

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: Before we go further — what are your compensation expectations?

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Happy to discuss. What is the band for the role?

lines.speaker: Recruiter
lines.text: We prefer to hear the candidate number first so we can match it to the right level.

lines.speaker: Candidate
lines.text: Understood. My expectation is in the range of 85–95k.

specimens.reading: The number is required from one side and withheld by the other, and it is collected before the level is fixed. Both outcomes below follow from that ordering.

specimens.label: The two branches
specimens.context: the same question, two candidates, one week

lines.text: Quoted 95k — We are not able to proceed; the expectation is outside the range we have for this role.
Quoted 70k — Good news, we would like to move ahead. Based on the conversation we are looking at this as a mid-level hire rather than senior.

specimens.reading: A high number ends the process and a low one moves the level. There is no answer that leaves both the process and the grade untouched — which is what makes it a bind rather than a negotiation.

perspectives.sees: A request for a compensation expectation at the screen, and a band that is not stated in return.
perspectives.reads: The number is collected before the level is fixed, so it is an input to the level rather than an answer to it.
perspectives.does: Names a range without the band, without the level, and without knowing how many others in the pipeline have already named one.

perspectives.sees: A screening form with an expectations field that has to be filled before the candidate moves to the panel, and disclosure rules for the band that are set elsewhere.
perspectives.reads: The number is the cheapest available check on whether the process is viable, before panel time is spent on it.
perspectives.does: Asks for the number first and records it in the field, and says about the band exactly what is permitted at this stage.

perspectives.sees: A band per level and a rule about what may be said about it, both reviewed on a cycle measured in quarters.
perspectives.reads: A stated expectation is the input that places a candidate on the grid; a band stated first becomes the floor of every negotiation that follows.
perspectives.does: Publishes the band where a disclosure rule requires it and not elsewhere, and keeps levelling a decision separate from the number.

perspectives.sees: Postings in covered jurisdictions, which either carry a band or do not.
perspectives.reads: A published band is measurable and enforceable; the level a candidate will be assessed at is neither.
perspectives.does: Requires the band in the posting, which closes one branch of the bind and leaves the levelling branch untouched.
